I wrote this as a reply to another post in /v/movies, but I think the topic warrants its own discussion thread (especially considering the article I replied to wasn't very good, and not really worth upvoating, IMO)

Zootopia is not some SJW hit piece. It's not a PC indoctrination film. Yes: it deals with topics of what it means to integrate into society and how the reality of it differs from some idealized utopia, but it requires an active and narrowly focused lens to claim that it's pushing a liberal message or even has a particular political bent more intense than the relatively uncontroversial "you have to deal with multiple cultures, personalities, and problems in modern society. Don't judge a book by its cover." Claiming that it's remotely discussing Donald Trump or actual politics is even more ridiculous, and I think it's obvious to anyone who cares about analyzing film.

The heart of the film's message is that This is an age-old message in animated films that we've seen again and again, but with a refreshingly modern world and a genuinely enjoyable buddy-cop/film-noir mystery to emotionally connect with.

The social themes in the movie are generally subdued and are in service to the story itself. It's also noteworthy that it pales in comparison not just to the enjoyable story, but to the sheer artistry in what is one of the best animated movies in years. The art direction, animation, lighting, and world building are all fantastic, and interaction of the two main characters is entertaining, funny, and at times touching.

When I saw the trailers I was actually anticipating (and worried) that they'd go in the SJW/PC nonsense direction. I expected nonstop messages of "women can do anything and it's not a man's world!" and "don't be racist!" and "stereotypes are bad!"; the trailers even took the scenes that focused on this the most and made it seem the movie was going to be aggressive and preachy and over the top. When I sat down to watch it, however, it became apparent that they were doing something much more artistic, non-preachy, and nuanced than this.

TL;DR: Zootopia's a fantastic animated movie, isn't preachy, blatant, or even necessarily PC, and it's almost guaranteed to be enjoyable to everyone who appreciates a good story and characters. Interpreting it as some piece of liberal or SJW culture (let alone claiming it's about modern politics or Donald Trump/immigration/Muslims/etc!) is almost entirely unsupportable. Worse, it would be a shame to see a movie with this much talent and craft and only be able to try and wring out the most aggressive and narrowly political viewpoint you could. You'd be missing out on the true merit of one of the best animated movies in years.
[Discussion] Zootopia isn't an SJW hit piece. It isn't a PC indoctrination film. And it certainly isn't about Donald Trump or politics that go beyond an age-old and timeless commentary on society.
